sn23.1:2.1: For Māra’s mythic history, see [sn4.1:2.1](). Early Buddhist texts present Māra as both a deity of ill intent, and as a metaphor for the death, desire, and entrapment. This discourse highlights the literal meaning of his name.
sn23.1:2.3: Using “murder” here I try to maintain the pun.
sn23.1:3.11: For ogadha, BB changed his mind, see his note at AN 3.60.
